Cohort2Trajectory

Cohort2Trajectory turns cohort intervals into patient trajectories. The target cohort defines each patient’s observation period. State cohorts describe what happened during that period. The analyst defines those cohorts and decides which state takes priority when records overlap.

The package accepts cohorts generated in an OMOP Common Data Model database, an R data frame or a CSV file. It produces either fixed-length cycles or continuous intervals. It does not infer diagnoses, recovery or a history state from the names of the supplied cohorts.

Start here

The documentation site contains the function reference and these articles:

  • Getting started: a small example that needs no database.
  • Configure a study: observation bounds, selection rules and overlapping states.
  • Import cohort data: local data, ATLAS definitions and saved studies.
  • Create trajectories: discrete and continuous output.
  • A weekly worked example: pneumonia history, two death states and a saved-study rerun.
  • Read the output: columns, dates, saved files and downstream use.

The usual workflow has three steps:

study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "MyStudy",
  pathToStudy = tempdir(),
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = input,
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 7
)

getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)

Here input is your cohort table. It needs subject_id, cohort_definition_id, cohort_start_date and cohort_end_date. Use "0" for target-cohort rows and the clinical labels for state rows. Supply dates as Date values in R or YYYY-MM-DD in CSV. The getting-started article supplies a complete input table.

Use names such as "Discrete" and "Priority" for the public options. They ignore case and surrounding spaces. Numeric option codes are not accepted.

What the trajectory means

A discrete trajectory assigns one state to each cycle. A seven-day cycle has seven days, including both endpoints. The final cycle can be shorter. Its selected state does not mean that the patient spent every day in that state. For example, a death recorded within the week can determine the week’s label.

A continuous trajectory keeps selected interval dates. It does not fill gaps or move simultaneous records onto different dates. In either format, START and EXIT mark boundaries, not clinical states. OUT OF COHORT means that no state was selected for a discrete cycle. It does not mean observation ended.

Overlapping states can be combined with mergeStates = TRUE. Membership is stored explicitly. A label containing + is never split to guess its members. Use mergedState() when a particular combination needs different allowed destinations, absorbing status or a display label. The configuration article explains the inheritance rules and their limits.

Rerun a saved study

A successful import and trajectory run saves its rules in Settings/analysisSettings.rds. For CDM studies, this file also contains the cohort JSON definitions used during import.

Copy the completed study’s Settings folder to the new study folder. Do not copy Data when sharing a study because it contains patient-level records. For a CDM rerun, supply a connection to the new database:

study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "MyStudy",
  pathToStudy = "/new/location",
  runSavedStudy = TRUE
)
getDataForStudy(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = study)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = study)

There is no need to re-enter the analytical settings or connect to ATLAS. For local data, also set useCDM = FALSE and supply fresh input through trajectoryDataObject or pathToData. To change the analysis rules, configure a new run instead of overriding a saved study.

Only the current RDS format, version 4, is supported. Older studies must be reconfigured and rerun. Settings CSV files and the removed arguments mergeThreshold and updateAutomaticallyForMergedStates are not supported.

Database access

CDM studies use a CDMConnector connection. The database account needs read access to the required CDM and vocabulary tables, and permission to create and populate tables in the configured write schema. Start with a small cohort when checking a new server connection.

Related packages

  • CohortContrast
  • TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis
  • TrajectoryViz

These packages have separate interfaces. Do not assume that an older analysis package can read the current trajectory output without checking its expected column names and handling of boundary rows.

Haug M, Oja M, Pajusalu M, et al. Markov modeling for cost-effectiveness using federated health data network. Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association, 2024. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocae044.

When reporting an analysis, also record the package version or Git commit and retain the settings used for the run.
